heading: Tata Sons chairman vote: Chandrasekaran reappointment ‘void ab initio’; Tata Trusts says resolution 'not validly passed' | Company Business News
paragraphs: Tata Trusts has reiterated its stance that the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as the Chairman of Tata Sons, which was approved by the latter's board on 17 September, was invalid since the required support of Tata Trusts’ nominee directors was not secured.

As per Tata Trusts, the Articles of Association (AoA) of Tata Sons says that a majority of the directors nominated by the trust has to approve the appointment or re-appointment of the chairperson. Tata Trusts is the majority shareholder (owns 66%) of the conglomerate. Since there are two nominees of Tata Trusts on the board of Tata Sons, both of them would have to support the resolution in order for the same to be considered passed.

It also said that the casting vote of the Chairman cannot be used to overcome the failure of this condition since such a vote becomes available only when it comes to equality of votes at the overall board level, and cannot be applied when the requirement concerns the nominee directors of Tata Trusts.

Tata Trusts rejected the claim because the required support from both of its nominee directors was not obtained, violating the Articles of Association that mandate majority approval from Tata Trusts' nominees.
The Articles of Association require that a majority of Tata Trusts' nominee directors approve the reappointment of the chairman for it to be considered valid.

During the voting, four directors supported Chandrasekaran's reappointment while one, Noel Tata, opposed it, which rendered the resolution invalid because it lacked majority support from the Tata Trusts' nominees.

Tata Trusts stated that the resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran is void ab initio, meaning it has no legal effect due to the failure to meet the necessary conditions set forth in the Articles of Association.

The casting vote of the chairman is not applicable because it can only be used to break ties at the overall board level, and not to satisfy the specific requirement for Tata Trusts' nominee directors.

"The Chairman's casting vote is available only where there is equality of votes at the overall board level. It does not apply amongst Tata Trusts' Nominee Directors," it said. "There was no paralysis, and there was no deadlock. The Board put a question, and the AoA answered it in the negative. The exercise of a protective right conferred by a company's own constitution is not a deadlock; it is that constitution working as it was written to work."

Since one of the two nominees voted against the reappointment of Chandrasekaran, "The resolution to reappoint Mr N. Chandrasekaran as the Chairman of Tata Sons, considered at the Board meeting on September 17, 2026, was not validly passed and has no legal effect. In the eyes of the law, it is void ab initio," Tata Trusts said in a statement.

"There are two Tata Trusts nominees on the Board of Tata Sons. Majority amongst two is two and not one," the Trusts also said. "On September 17, 2026, one such Director voted against the resolution. Thus, the affirmative support of Tata Trusts Nominee Directors as mandated by the AoA was not given. The condition failed, and so did the resolution."

The board of Tata Sons had voted 4-1 in favour of Chandrasekaran being given another five-year extension as its chairman. with the only opposing vote being cast by Noel Tata. The other nominee of the Tata Trusts, Venu Srinivasan, had supported Chandrasekaran's extension.
"Whether the result of the vote was 4:1, or any other figure, is irrelevant. A condition is either met, or it is not. In this case the condition was not met," the Trusts said.
